title: Rural water infrastructure can be financially available while the path to funding remains unusable
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107355 review of USDA and EPA assistance for rural unserved water and wastewater communities
geography: United States; rural unserved communities, 10 selected states, three site-visit states, and one Tribe

observations.period: 2022-December 2025 program and community review; published June 2026

denominator.unit: USDA and EPA programs identified as able to provide financial or technical assistance

assistance_programs.unit: programs offering financial or technical assistance

data_boundary.value: USDA and EPA had limited data on rural unserved communities but could obtain some information through programs and datasets

application_complexity.value: communities often needed multiple applications across federal and state sources with different deadlines and use restrictions

funding_timing.value: one community did not receive a federal grant in time to obtain a matching state grant

coordination_status.value: USDA and EPA had not updated and monitored their 2017 joint memorandum

local_knowledge.value: EPA technical-assistance providers lacked agency guidance ensuring awareness of local capacity and incorporation of local knowledge

observations.method: GAO reviewed USDA and EPA program documents and data, interviewed federal officials and officials from 10 selected states, and visited rural unserved communities in three states and one Tribe.
observations.uncertainty: The review identifies program and access barriers but does not estimate the share of unserved communities that fail to obtain assistance, the causal effect of coordination, or household-level health outcomes. Selected states and site visits are not a national probability sample.
observations.subgroup: Rural unserved communities, unincorporated areas, small utilities, Tribes, state and local applicants, federal technical-assistance providers, and communities with limited financial or administrative capacity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Multiple programs and technical assistance can still provide real routes to infrastructure, and a missed match example does not establish a general failure rate. Communities may use local, state, private, or onsite solutions not captured as one federal funding path.

related_sources.claim: The full GAO report contains program tables, community profiles, project-cost information, and methodology.

boundary: This record measures whether rural communities can identify and navigate federal and state financial or technical assistance for water infrastructure. It does not establish that a community received an award, built a system, obtained safe water or wastewater service, reduced household costs, or improved health.
